headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Great Expectations outputs feeding Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing/search workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can emit validation results and documentation files, and Perplexity ingests uploaded documents plus browsing context. If GE output is copied into Perplexity, attacker-controlled text in reports could steer prompts. The pair lacks a documented isolation/provenance layer, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are pasted or uploaded into Perplexity as analysis input
IF validation reports contain untrusted text that Perplexity treats as instructions
mitigations: Strip instructions from GE reports before upload
Use a fixed report template with quoted-only excerpts
Add a manual review step before Perplexity ingestion
Tag untrusted sections as data, not prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, while Perplexity uploads documents and sends queries to vendor APIs/search providers. If GE artifacts include sensitive data and are uploaded to Perplexity, that data can leave the local environment. GE has no network egress, but Perplexity’s vendor-hosted processing makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF GE validation artifacts contain sensitive rows or identifiers
IF those artifacts are uploaded to Perplexity for analysis
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before upload
Limit uploads to synthetic samples
Review Perplexity privacy settings before use
Keep GE outputs in a separate workspace
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploaded documents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write files in its own workflow, while Perplexity cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shell. The pair therefore has little direct write-write conflict; any overlap is mainly through user-managed files, not simultaneous mutable control.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF the operator manually copies Perplexity outputs into files GE also manages
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Avoid letting Perplexity edit repo files
Run GE in a locked workspace
Review file diffs before committing
requires-engineering: add orchestration locks around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: GE produces validation results that Perplexity can summarize or cite in downstream answers. Perplexity’s browsing/search workflow may treat those outputs as authoritative unless the operator verifies them, creating a plausible chain from analysis to mistaken action. The pair does not show automatic action-taking, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Perplexity is asked to restate or act on GE validation results
IF the operator relies on Perplexity without checking the underlying GE run
mitigations: Require source links in Perplexity answers
Compare claims against the original GE report
Use a second reviewer for critical findings
Mark GE outputs as provisional until verified
requires-engineering: add automated result verification before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations handles data quality tests, validation results, and documentation locally, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents through vendor-hosted services and search providers. If regulated or sensitive data is included in GE artifacts and then uploaded, retention/residency terms may differ. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in GE artifacts
IF those artifacts are uploaded to Perplexity without a governing DPA or residency review
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from uploads
Check Perplexity retention settings
Use anonymized validation outputs
Document approved data classes for each tool
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement and residency review
